keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (no Cliopatria row). The page gives no area and names no towns of the territory; a 100 km radius round the capital is my reading. Cliopatria draws the Chernigov row to 1240 and no row for 1241-1293; the page says the principality was later taken by Briansk after the Mongol invasions (page, paraphrased) and then by Lithuania (undated, 'citation needed'), so the extent over 1240-1503 is not known.

ledger.note: 1097: Novgorod-Seversk becomes a principality of the Chernigov dynasty. The infobox gives 'Established: 1097' and 'Personal union with the Principality of Chernigov'; the page names Sviatoslav Olgovich as founder of the local Olgovichi branch but gives no year for him.

region.text: the Seversk land round Novgorod-Seversk, originally a subdivision of Chernigov, with territories formerly part of Chernigov and Pereyaslavl (page, paraphrased)

ledger.note: 25 March 1503: Novgorod-Seversk passes to Moscow. 'a six-year truce was concluded on the Feast of the Annunciation (March 25) in 1503'; Lithuania lost 'Chernigov, Novgorod-Seversk, Starodub, and lands around the upper Oka River'; the Novgorod-Seversk infobox gives 'Disestablished: 1503'.

wars.outcome: Hostilities renewed in May 1500; Lithuania was beaten at Vedrosha on 14 July 1500 and the truce of 25 March 1503 left Moscow Chernigov, Novgorod-Seversk, Starodub and the upper Oka.
wars.note: The page does not mention a defection of the Seversk princes, so the principality's own part in 1500 is not recorded here.

wars.name: Igor Svyatoslavich's campaign against the Cumans (1185)
wars.outcome: 'Ended in defeat for Prince Igor of Novgorod-Seversk', recorded in The Tale of Igor's Campaign; no change of border.

certainty.note: No boundary or town list on the page; a radius round the capital.

notes: New state flagged by eu-16-b (Chernigov). Two pages (page budget). The Russo-Lithuanian War article of that name does not exist; the war is on 'Muscovite-Lithuanian Wars'. The state lived as an apanage in personal union with Chernigov (to 1240), then taken by Briansk after the Mongol invasions (page, paraphrased) and by Lithuania, neither dated on the page, so no gain or loss is entered between 1097 and 1503 and the extent is a single radius. It overlaps principality-of-chernigov (to 1240) and later Lithuanian and Muscovite shapes; the renderer should draw it only where those are absent, or a gap-filler may fold it into Chernigov. The 1206-1212 reign of Igor's sons in Halych (page) is a Halych matter. Wikidata id unknown.
